    Factor Analytic Selection Tools: FAST and iClass Analysis

    fastIC.Rd

    A unified implementation of the FAST (Factor Analytic Selection Tools; Smith & Cullis 2018) and iClass (interaction class; Smith et al. 2021) approaches for summarising variety performance from a Factor Analytic Linear Mixed Model fitted in ASReml-R V4.

    Both methods build on the rotated FA loadings \(\hat{\bm{\Lambda}}\) and score EBLUPs \(\hat{\bm{f}}\) returned by faSummary(). The Common Variety Effect (CVE) for genotype \(g\) in environment \(j\) is the FA regression prediction:

    $$ \widehat{\text{CVE}}(g,j) = \sum_{r=1}^{k} \hat{\lambda}_{rj}\,\hat{f}_{rg} $$

    The Variance Accounted For (VAF) by each factor in environment \(j\) is \(\hat{\lambda}_{rj}^2 / (\sum_r \hat{\lambda}_{rj}^2 + \hat{\psi}_j)\), and the specific variance accounts for the remainder; see plot_faSummary() with type = "VAF" for a per-environment visualisation.

    Usage

    fastIC(model, term = "fa(Site, 4):Genotype", ic.num = 2L, ...)

    Arguments

    model

    An ASReml-R V4 model object containing a Factor Analytic random term.

    term

    Character string identifying the FA random term, written as "fa(<EnvFactor>, k):<GenotypeFactor>". The genotype factor may be wrapped in vm(...) (pedigree/genomic models) or ide(...) (identity relationship matrix) for relationship-aware models. Default "fa(Site, 4):Genotype".

    ic.num

    Integer. Number of factors used to form iClasses and compute iClassOP. Must be strictly less than \(k\) (i.e. between 1 and \(k - 1\)) so that the kth factor remains available for iClassRMSD. Default 2.

    ...

    Additional arguments forwarded to faSummary().

    Value

    A data frame with one row per environment \(\times\) genotype combination, sorted by iclass then environment then genotype, containing:

    <EnvFactor>

    Environment labels.

    <GenotypeFactor>

    Genotype labels.

    loads1, ..., loadsK

    Rotated FA loadings per environment.

    spec.var

    Specific (residual) genetic variance per environment.

    score1, ..., scoreK

    Rotated FA score EBLUPs per genotype.

    fitted1, ..., fittedK

    Per-factor contributions to CVE: \(\hat{\lambda}_{rj}\hat{f}_{rg}\).

    CVE

    Common Variety Effect (sum of all fitted values).

    global_op

    Global Overall Performance (FAST): repeated for every environment row of a genotype.

    global_dev

    Residual from first-factor regression (FAST): \(\widehat{\text{CVE}} - \hat{\lambda}_{1j}\hat{f}_{1g}\). Only present when \(k > 1\).

    global_stab

    RMSD of global_dev across all environments (FAST stability): repeated for every environment row of a genotype. Only present when \(k > 1\).

    iclass

    Sign-pattern iClass label for the environment.

    iClassOP

    Within-iClass Overall Performance for the genotype.

    iClassRMSD

    Within-iClass RMSD for the genotype.

    Two attributes are attached to the returned data frame for use by plot_fastIC() with type = "VAF":

    vaf_env

    Data frame with one row per environment containing the proportion of genetic variance accounted for by each factor (Factor1, ..., FactorK) and the specific variance (Specific), plus the total genetic variance (total_var) for that environment.

    vaf_summary

    Data frame with one row per source (Factor 1, ..., Factor K, Specific) containing the overall proportion of total genetic variance (pct_var) and cumulative proportion (cum_pct).

    Unified framework

    FAST and iClass are treated as a single framework. FAST global metrics are computed unconditionally across all environments; iClass metrics partition environments by the sign pattern of the first ic.num rotated loadings and compute within-class analogues. When ic.num = 1 and all first-factor loadings are positive (the typical outcome after rotation), there is exactly one iClass and iClassOP equals global_op while iClassRMSD equals global_stab — the two frameworks agree. When ic.num >= 2 the environments split into multiple classes and the iClass metrics diverge from the global ones, revealing crossover GEI that FAST alone cannot detect.

    Global FAST metrics

    After rotation the first factor captures the dominant non-crossover genotype-environment interaction (GEI) pattern and typically has all-positive loadings. The global metrics summarise each genotype across all environments:

    global_op

    \(\text{global\_op}(g) = \bar{\lambda}_1 \cdot \hat{f}_{1g}\), where \(\bar{\lambda}_1 = t^{-1}\sum_j\hat{\lambda}_{1j}\). On the same scale as the trait; the genotype's expected performance at the average environment.

    global_dev

    \(\text{global\_dev}(g,j) = \widehat{\text{CVE}}(g,j) - \hat{\lambda}_{1j}\hat{f}_{1g}\): residual from the first-factor regression. Only present when \(k > 1\).

    global_stab

    \(\text{global\_stab}(g) = \sqrt{t^{-1}\sum_j \text{global\_dev}(g,j)^2}\): RMSD of the first-factor residual across all environments. A small value indicates broad adaptation. Only present when \(k > 1\).

    iClass metrics

    Environments are grouped by the sign pattern of their first ic.num rotated loadings:

    $$ \text{iClass}(j) = \bigotimes_{r=1}^{\texttt{ic.num}} \begin{cases} \text{p} & \hat{\lambda}_{rj} \ge 0 \\ \text{n} & \hat{\lambda}_{rj} < 0 \end{cases} $$

    Within each iClass \(\omega\):

    iClassOP

    \(\text{iClassOP}(g,\omega) = \sum_{r=1}^{\texttt{ic.num}} \bar{\lambda}_{r\omega} \cdot \hat{f}_{rg}\), where \(\bar{\lambda}_{r\omega}\) is the mean of factor \(r\)'s loadings across environments in \(\omega\).

    iClassRMSD

    \(\text{iClassRMSD}(g,\omega) = \sqrt{|\omega|^{-1} \sum_{j\in\omega} \text{dev}_{ic}(g,j)^2}\), where \(\text{dev}_{ic}(g,j) = \widehat{\text{CVE}}(g,j) - \sum_{r=1}^{\texttt{ic.num}} \hat{\lambda}_{rj}\hat{f}_{rg}\). The kth factor is reserved for this residual; therefore ic.num must be strictly less than \(k\).

    References

    Smith, A.B. & Cullis, B.R. (2018). Plant breeding selection tools built on factor analytic mixed models for multi-environment trial data. Euphytica, 214, 143.

    Smith, A.B., Norman, A., Kuchel, H. & Cullis, B.R. (2021). Plant variety selection using interaction classes derived from factor analytic linear mixed models: models with independent variety effects. Frontiers in Plant Science, 12, 737462.
